title: BOSS: Blocking algorithm for optimizing shuttling scheduling in Ion Trap
problem: Shuttling operations in ion trap quantum computers cause significant fidelity loss and elongated execution times, particularly as circuit sizes grow to 4000+ two-qubit gates across 64-78 qubits.
method: BOSS is a blocking algorithm that groups quantum operations into blocks to reduce the total number of shuttle operations required during circuit execution. The algorithm is evaluated on realistic experimental parameters incorporating sympathetic cooling for higher fidelity and more accurate execution time estimation. Experiments cover circuits with up to 4000+ two-qubit gates and 64-78 qubits.

title: PracMHBench: Re-evaluating Model-Heterogeneous Federated Learning Based on Practical Edge Device Constraints
problem: Model-heterogeneous federated learning (allowing different model architectures per device) is more practical than homogeneous FL, but existing algorithms have not been rigorously evaluated against real edge device constraints and resource limitations.
method: PracMHBench constructs a system platform to evaluate model-heterogeneous FL algorithms under practical edge device constraints, classifying diverse heterogeneity algorithms and testing on multiple data tasks and resource constraint scenarios.

title: Concord: Rethinking Distributed Coherence for Software Caches in Serverless Environments
problem: Serverless functions incur high latency from frequent global storage accesses; existing node-local caching schemes either restrict each data item to a single cache node (causing frequent remote reads) or allow multi-node replication but impose heavy coherence overhead, neither being optimal for serverless access patterns characterized by frequent reads, strong temporal locality, and few concurrent writers.
method: Concord implements a directory-based distributed software cache coherence protocol inspired by hardware cache coherence, adapted for serverless environments. It allows multiple replicas of the same data item across nodes and satisfies reads locally from any replica. To maintain coherence, a directory tracks replica locations and manages invalidation/update messages on writes. The protocol minimizes coherence traffic by exploiting serverless access patterns, reduces contention points in the directory, and handles node failures and frequent coherence domain changes (as serverless function instances spin up/down). Two additional capabilities are unlocked: transactional storage accesses and transparent data-aware function placement.

title: A Single-Inductor-Based High-Voltage Transmit Beamformer for Wearable Ultrasound Devices Achieving 88% fCV2 Power Reduction
problem: Wearable ultrasound transducer arrays for vagus nerve stimulation suffer from excessive power loss from charging/discharging transducer capacitance (fCV² loss); prior resonant pulsers require multiple off-chip inductors, incompatible with miniaturized form factors.
method: A single-inductor resonant transmit beamformer architecture pulses groups of transducer elements at different phases from a shared inductor, enabling energy recycling across the array while avoiding the complex body-diode losses of prior approaches.

title: H2-LLM: Hardware-Dataflow Co-Exploration for Heterogeneous Hybrid-Bonding-based Low-Batch LLM Inference
problem: Edge-side low-batch LLM inference (personal assistant, reception bot, private edge server) is bottlenecked by the DRAM bandwidth wall: existing NMP designs embed compute engines inside DRAM dies, limiting compute capacity and creating an imbalance between bandwidth and computation for both prefill (compute-bound) and decoding (bandwidth-bound) stages. Hybrid-bonding technology offers a path to higher compute capacity near memory, but the trade-off between computation capacity and bandwidth has not been systematically explored.
method: H2-LLM proposes a hybrid-bonding-based heterogeneous accelerator that places high-capacity compute dies in face-to-face contact with DRAM dies, exploiting the high through-silicon-via bandwidth of hybrid bonding. The architecture exposes a design space covering compute tile counts, memory bandwidth allocation, and die partitioning. A data-centric dataflow abstraction is introduced to map LLM operations (attention, feed-forward, KV-cache access) onto the heterogeneous on-die and near-die compute resources across both prefill and decoding stages. A design space exploration (DSE) framework automatically searches this joint architecture-dataflow space for the Pareto-optimal configuration.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Energy Management for Wearable IoT Devices with Conformal Prediction
problem: Energy management for battery-powered wearable IoT devices with stochastic ambient energy harvesting; existing point-prediction energy management methods do not account for prediction uncertainty.
method: Conformal prediction framework for future energy harvest that provides prediction intervals with provable coverage guarantees. Uncertainty regions are leveraged in a Monte Carlo sampling-based energy management algorithm that evaluates multiple decisions across sampled energy scenarios; results are aggregated via lightweight ML model to make near-optimal energy decisions.

title: MIRACLE: Multimodal Information Retrieval via a Combined In-Memory Processing and Content Addressable Memory Approach
problem: Multimodal retrieval via neural feature extraction + similarity search is inefficient; cosine similarity on von Neumann wastes memory bandwidth, and pure hashing sacrifices accuracy due to modal heterogeneity.
method: Hybrid architecture combining in-memory random hashing (PIM) for fast approximate ranking and content-addressable memory (CAM) for parallel search space reduction, followed by final cosine reranking for accuracy recovery.

title: ORCHES: Orchestrated Test-Time-Compute-based LLM Reasoning on Collaborative GPU-PIM HEterogeneous System
problem: Test-time compute (TTC) inference pipelines for LLM reasoning on edge devices suffer from three bottlenecks: variable parallelism due to inference-dependent dynamic control flow and varying batch sizes; branch dependencies that stall sequential reasoning steps; and branch pruning causing memory fragmentation and irregular access patterns.
method: ORCHES is a GPU-PIM collaborative system that partitions LLM reasoning workloads between a GPU and Processing-in-Memory (PIM) units. Three key mechanisms address the identified bottlenecks: (1) adaptive workload assignment dynamically balances computation between GPU and PIM based on real-time branching patterns; (2) branch-aware pipelining uses speculative execution to overlap reasoning steps and reduce inter-step pipeline stalls from branch dependencies; (3) fragmentation-aware memory structuring improves data locality through coordinated caching strategies and optimized memory layout reorganization to handle irregular access caused by branch pruning.

title: MetaDSE: A Few-shot Meta-learning Framework for Cross-workload CPU Design Space Exploration
problem: Cross-workload CPU design space exploration suffers from overfitting, data ambiguity, and workload dissimilarity when leveraging transfer learning.
method: MetaDSE reframes cross-workload CPU DSE as a few-shot meta-learning problem using model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML). It introduces a workload-adaptive architectural mask algorithm to uncover inherent architectural properties across diverse workloads.

title: 37.2 A 2-Dimensional mm-Scale Network-on-Textiles (kNOTs) for Wearable Computing with Direct Die-to-Yarn Integration of 0.6×2.15mm2 SoC and bySPI Chiplets
problem: E-textile systems require highly miniaturized, flexible SoCs that seamlessly integrate into garments while supporting heterogeneous sensing, computation, and distributed memory—prior work trades off bulk, cost, 1D networks, or lacks integrated SoCs.
method: kNOT (Network-on-Textiles) integrates two miniaturized chiplets directly into braided composite yarns: (1) a 0.6×2.15mm² SoC with reconfigurable pads, fault-tolerant bootup, clock synchronization, and dynamic network config; (2) a bySPI chiplet (bypass-SPI enhancement) enabling multi-receiver connectivity with only 3 wires. Direct die-to-yarn integration via selective laser ablation and solder reflow avoids bulky interposers.

title: A Crystal-Less Frequency-Modulation Transmitter IC with Joint Neural-Network-Driven Modulation and Coding for Low-Power Connectivity
problem: IoT transmitters suffer from high power consumption and complexity of PLL-based frequency modulation requiring crystal references, while crystal-less alternatives suffer carrier drift, phase noise, or need additional resonant devices.
method: Crystal-less FM transmitter using free-running LC oscillator with neural-network-driven modulation and coding jointly optimizing the transmit waveform to compensate for oscillator drift and phase noise while maintaining link reliability.

title: SSDL-ILT: Efficient ILT utilizing a self-supervised deep learning model
problem: Inverse lithography technology (ILT) for mask optimization is hindered by time-intensive physical simulation; pixel-level mask optimization requires expensive iterative refinement.
method: Proposes self-supervised deep learning model for ILT with novel loss function guiding training without labeled data; model outputs final mask patterns directly, auto-generates sub-resolution assist features (SRAFs) with adjustable complexity.

title: Debugger Toolchain Validation via Cross-Level Debugging
problem: Existing debugger toolchain validation techniques detect bugs in debug information by comparing execution traces between optimized and unoptimized executables, but compiler optimizations make such traces incomparable and leave bugs in debugger toolchains undetected when the unoptimized executable itself contains toolchain errors.
method: The paper introduces Cross-Level Debugging (CLD), which compares execution traces obtained from debugging the same executable using source-level and instruction-level debugging strategies within the same debugger. CLD formalizes three invariant relations—reachability preservation of program locations, order preservation for reachable locations, and value consistency at program locations—that must hold between the two trace levels regardless of optimization level. The Devil framework implements these relations as test oracles, generates diverse test programs, runs them under both debugging levels, and flags violations as toolchain bugs.

title: 19.6 A 60GHz I/Q-Calibrated SSB-Mixer-Based LO with Sub-ns Settling Time and -56dBc Worst-Case Spur Using ILO Filter in 28nm CMOS
problem: Joint Communication-and-Sensing (JCAS) systems using SC-OFDM (stepped-carrier OFDM) require local oscillators (LOs) with fast frequency-hopping settling (<18ns for IEEE 802.11ay) and low spurious tones; traditional LOs cannot meet both stringent jitter and settling requirements simultaneously.
method: 60GHz SSB (single-sideband) mixer-based LO with integrated LC oscillator (ILO) filter; achieves sub-ns settling via rapid frequency-hop architecture and I/Q calibration to suppress spurs to -56dBc worst-case.

title: Marching Page Walks: Batching and Concurrent Page Table Walks for Enhancing GPU Throughput
problem: GPU page table walkers handle only a single walk request at a time, creating severe queuing latency when thousands of concurrent threads simultaneously demand address translation across wide virtual address ranges.
method: Marching Page Walks (MPW) scans the pool of pending walk requests to identify groups that can share memory accesses (e.g., walks to nearby pages sharing a page table entry lookup). It batches these requests and concurrently issues multiple memory instructions per walker to service several walks simultaneously, exploiting the observation that GPU workloads access pages in wide but often co-located address ranges.

title: AmpereBleed: Exploiting On-chip Current Sensors for Circuit-Free Attacks on ARM-FPGA SoCs
problem: FPGAs are vulnerable to power side-channel attacks; existing attacks require assumptions of co-resident crafted circuits and shared power delivery networks, limiting practicality.
method: Proposes AmpereBleed, a current-based side-channel attack exploiting widely available INA226 current sensors in ARM-FPGA SoCs without requiring coresident circuits; uses sensor readings to fingerprint and attack victim workloads.
